inst_s1_b:
The «Chart settings» panel holds all the controls, and next to it a live preview updates automatically on every change. On wide screens the two sit side by side; on a phone they stack, with the preview below the settings.

Workflow: 1) choose a chart type; 2) enter a title and a dataset name; 3) fill in the data in the table below; 4) undo or redo if needed; 5) open «Export» to download an image or save the project.
inst_s2_b:
There are 29 types, grouped by how their data is entered:

  • Label / value: bar, line, area, horizontal bar, pie, doughnut, radar, polar area, word cloud.
  • X / Y points: scatter (X, Y), bubble (X, Y, size).
  • Several datasets: stacked, grouped, multi line, combo (each dataset is a bar or a line).
  • Category and value list: box plot, violin.
  • Hierarchy: treemap (label, value, group).
  • Grid: heatmap (X, Y, value).
  • Flows: sankey (from, to, flow).
  • Map: choropleth (country from a list, value).
  • Bar with error bars
  • Candlestick / OHLC
  • Funnel
  • Venn
  • Graph (network)
  • Gauge
  • Function (y = f(x))
inst_s3_b:
The data table adapts to the chosen type. «Add row» adds an entry, the cross removes one.

  • Label / value: a label and a number.
  • Points: X and Y (bubble also has size).
  • Several datasets: categories are comma-separated, each dataset's values are a comma-separated list of numbers; in combo each dataset is set to bar or line.
  • Box / violin: a comma-separated list of numbers in the values field.
  • Heatmap: X, Y (categories) and a value.
  • Sankey: from, to and the flow amount.
  • Choropleth: the country is picked from a dropdown (names in the interface language), plus a value.
  • Bar with error bars: Label, Value, Error.
  • Candlestick / OHLC: Date, O/H/L/C.
  • Funnel: Label, Value.
  • Venn: Sets (comma separated), Value.
  • Graph (network): Nodes (comma separated), From/To.
  • Gauge: Value, Max.
  • The Function type plots y = f(x). Enter an expression — e.g. sin(x), x^2, sqrt(x) — the X range (min and max) and the number of points. Function evaluates the expression and draws the curve; the formula also appears in the data list under the chart.
inst_s4_b:
The «Export» button opens a window.

  • Format: PNG, JPEG, WEBP, AVIF (a real format, encoded in the browser — the encoder loads on first use), SVG (vector) and PDF (a page the size of the image; the encoder loads on first use).
  • Width and height — the exact pixel size of the saved file; empty means the current chart size.
  • Include data — adds the list of data below the chart to the image.
  • Download image — saves the picture with an opaque background that matches the chart.
  • Print — opens the browser print dialog with the chart as an image; from there you can print it or choose «Save as PDF».
  • Save project — a .json file with all settings; the «Include history and journal» checkbox adds them to the file.
  • in combo/multi each dataset can use the left or right Y axis.
inst_s5_b: The «Import» button opens a window with a zone where you can drop a .json project file or click to select one. Once a file is chosen, the «Apply project» button becomes active and loads the settings (and the history and journal if they were saved).

inst_s7_b:
• Ctrl/Cmd + Z — undo
  • Ctrl/Cmd + Y or Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Z — redo
  • Ctrl/Cmd + S — save project
  • Ctrl/Cmd + E — export window
  • Ctrl/Cmd + O — import window
  • Ctrl/Cmd + J — journal
  • Ctrl/Cmd + , — settings

Inside input fields Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y work as normal text editing.
inst_s8_b:
• Undo / Redo: roll data and settings changes back and forward.
  • Journal: keeps actions, hints and errors; it can be cleared.
inst_s9_b:
The «Advanced» section above the data table groups optional settings: subtitle; line smoothing, stepped, dashed and filled lines; stacked and logarithmic Y axis; decimation; legend position; point size and line width; animation duration and easing; and on-demand effects — data labels, zoom/pan, annotations, trendline and crosshair. In combo and multi charts each dataset can use the left or right Y axis. Each option appears only for the types it applies to.

Colours. Under «Canvas background» you can set the background (transparent, a colour or an image) and override colours independently: the chart (series), the grid lines, the axis numbers and labels, the title, the dataset / legend text, and the data-list text and its background. «Reset» returns every colour to the theme. All of these are saved in the project.
